title: Planet State v1
description:
One frame of a planet, shaped for a tile renderer rather than for a browser. The campaign simulation serves this over HTTP and the client polls it; the client never writes back through this channel, and nothing here enters a match - a battle is set up once from a battle-request-v1 document and is deterministic from that point on. Keeping the two apart is what lets the campaign be floating-point Python and the battle be integer lockstep.

Cells are flat arrays in row-major order, latitude-major, which is the layout a tile map wants and avoids ten thousand JSON objects per frame.

step.description: Campaign step, which is one day. The client uses it to tell a new frame from a repeat.

cells.description: Every array is latitudeCells * longitudeCells long, row-major, north to south. Quantised to small integers on purpose: this is polled about once a second and a full-precision float grid would be several megabytes a frame for detail no tile can show.

biome.description: Terrain class the tileset maps to. Derived from temperature, moisture and standing biomass, so a battle fought on a cell is fought on the ground the physics produced there.

biomass.description: Standing biomass, 0-255. What the hive is there to eat, and what is left after it has.

population.description: Occupancy relative to a fully settled cell, 0-255, saturating. Density spans orders of magnitude, so this is a log scale and not a linear one.

temperatureK.description: Rounded to whole kelvin. Enough for a heat overlay and for choosing a tileset.

factions.description: Enough to label and colour what the cell array points at.

colour.description: RRGGBB, matching how the mod already writes player colours.

race.description: Present once a race has woken. Traits are multipliers around 1.0, read off the world that raised it.
